people_partner.text: Putting comp and retention on the record: PACKET FACT the band is '$231,000 – $340,000 base, plus equity and bonus' with 'BAND STRETCH: not stated in the JD... treat $340K as the top,' and the role's own LEVEL line calls this 'senior-to-staff IC' — yet the candidate's demonstrated scope is 'Senior Research Scientist,' 'RLHF Team Lead' at HuggingFace, 'co-leading Olmo' at AI2, first-author on Tulu 3 (1481 cites) and RewardBench, plus a 40,357-follower public platform and Congressional testimony on open models. INFERENCE (BACKGROUND: senior/staff research profiles with team-lead or co-lead titles, flagship first-author papers, and this level of public visibility typically command well above $340K base at comparable well-funded AI companies, before equity): this reads as beyond-stretch, not within-stretch over-experience, and nothing in the role file signals the hiring manager will move the band that far for a no-reports IC seat. That comp gap combines with the title drop from team-lead/co-lead to IC and a seat with no stated growth path back into leadership — the hard-flag combination my lens is built to name — and it sits on top of a founder ambition that is evidenced rather than assumed ('I'm starting a new research organization around open language models,' present tense, plus 'my first research intern'), which is itself the primary 24-month retention driver, alongside seat size (no reports, no path back to leading an org) and the comp gap; Seattle-versus-SF-hybrid is a secondary driver. I'm moving from 'Not assessable' to Misaligned on the comp/seat-fit axis specifically — capability was never in question — while the recruiter-call question of whether he's actually available (live venture vs. paused, and why he'd trade it for this seat) stays open and unresolved by anything currently on record.

ai_evaluator.text: Two-worlds on the agent-harness gap, as I was called on to resolve: World A, real gap — his entire demonstrated arc (Tulu 3, RewardBench, OLMo family, TRL co-authorship, rlhf-book) is single-turn/generative post-training and reward modeling on static completions, and AI2/HF are open-model research labs whose benchmarks never required tool-use, subagent, or retrieval-harness engineering, so it plausibly just never entered his work. World B, unrepresented — Scholar's own header says 'Articles 1-20... this is the top 20 by citation count, not the complete record,' 'No README text captured for any repo' across all 26 listed, and his most recent public output ('Spurious rewards: Rethinking training signals in rlvr,' and the 1-week-old post: 'We did this: If your GRPO group has all wrong completions, sample more with probability P (~0.9)... in search of more GRPO batches with nonzero gradient') is exactly the RL-on-verifiable-multi-step-tasks technique family that agent-harness tuning for long-horizon work is typically built from, and none of it is captured under his current stealth headline ('Building Open Language Models @ (stealth)') at all. I split this roughly 35/65 toward 'unrepresented': the packet's structural blind spots on this specific axis (citation-sorted Scholar hides recent low-cited work, zero README/commit content for any repo, total silence on the stealth org's actual work) are severe enough, and his 2025-2026 RLVR/GRPO trajectory close enough to the harness discipline, that 'not visible' reads as ABSENCE OF EVIDENCE rather than EVIDENCE OF ABSENCE here — a correction to my own turn-8 framing, where I called it 'no visible footprint at Build depth' without weighing how thin the packet specifically is on his last two years. The single separating question: has he, in the stealth org or in work Scholar's citation-sort buries, built or tuned a multi-step agentic system — tools, subagents, retrieval, validation loops — as opposed to single-turn post-training and reward modeling on static completions; note also that this sits outside the JD's strict three-part disambiguation test (weight-changing post-training, trace-level judgment, production Python), which he still plausibly clears, so even a real harness gap would leave him inside the role's core triad, just short on one piece of its broader mandate.

senior_engineer.text: Final classification against the disambiguation triad: weight-changing post-training is OWNED (Tulu 3 first-author, 'RLHF Team Lead' at HF, 'co-leading Olmo' at AI2, RewardBench first-author, the 1-week-old GRPO post); grader/reward-as-first-class-artefact is OWNED ('RewardBench: Evaluating reward models' is literally the JD's grader-craft language applied to reward models); trace-level judgment is OWNED on generative completions and reward-model preference data but Not Visible on multi-step agent transcripts; harness-as-tunable-surface is Not Visible, and I agree with ai_evaluator that for the stealth-org window specifically this reads as packet-thin rather than demonstrated-absent, since that employer is one headline with no work content. Production research Python is the leg still Unverifiable, and contra a 'blind on last two years' framing, that specific gap is not a recency problem: 'No README text captured for any repo' spans all 26 listed repos across his whole career, TRL is sixth-of-six-author co-authorship with no described contribution, dgx-spark-setup is confirmed Shell not Python, and his own original Python repos (dynamicslearn, mbrl-lib, continuousprediction) are pre-LLM PhD robotics work rather than post-training code — so this is a packet-capture failure on the entire record, making it a genuine blocking artefact for the JD's explicit 'research engineer, not research scientist' non-negotiable, not a screen-call nicety. Verdict stays Unverifiable - request code, confidence 60; the artefact that resolves it either way is a commit, PR diff, or source file he personally authored — in TRL, a Tulu/OLMo post-training recipe, or rlhf-book.

engineering_manager.text: These aren't the same standard applied inconsistently — they're two different claims at two different grains, and the packet's density differs across them. ai_evaluator's harness question is a narrow technical-activity claim scoped to specific recent months at one employer whose entire content is a headline, 'Building Open Language Models @ (stealth)' — zero lines describing the actual work, so that window really is ABSENCE OF EVIDENCE. The cost/latency/security/governance question is coarser: it asks what kind of organization he's worked for, and the packet gives complete title-plus-description coverage across every disclosed employer since 2017 — DeepMind internship ('Working with the controls team on robotics, RL'), Hugging Face ('RLHF team-lead'), AI2 ('in the open and for the common good'), and his own newsletter ('Cutting edge AI research and news in your inbox') — none framed as commercial-product-constrained work, and that pattern holds across 8+ years and five distinct employers, not one thin recent line. So I stand on EVIDENCE OF ABSENCE for environment match — the packet is detailed enough, at the grain that claim needs, for a paying-customer shipping environment to show if it existed, and it doesn't — while conceding ai_evaluator is right that the fine-grained harness-engineering question is unresolved because the one employer where it might live has no content at all. Verdict stays Screen, confidence 44; technical ramp 6-10 weeks, with availability/comp and regime-fit — not capability — the open risk.

science_lead.text: Conceding the correction without argument: the Scholar list has three first-author papers, not two — 'Low Level Control of a Quadrotor with Deep Model-Based Reinforcement Learning' (N Lambert first author, 267 cites, 2019) sits alongside Tülu 3 and RewardBench. It doesn't move my independence read, because it's PhD-era work under a named advisor committee (Calandra, Pister, with Levine and Tomlin on committee) — exactly the kind of first-author-but-advisor-agenda output my independence test is built to discount — whereas Tülu 3 and RewardBench came after the RLHF-team-lead and Olmo-co-lead titles, which is the actual independence signal. On engineering_manager's line, it holds and I can't resolve it from my evidence: Tülu 3 and RewardBench demonstrate novelty and rigor-by-proxy in the research-shipping discipline — recipe design, grader-as-artefact, citation velocity — but nothing in the 20-paper Scholar list, the repos, or the GRPO post shows him ever trading model quality against cost, latency, security, or governance for a paying customer; a packet this dense (full job history since 2017, an About section, activity through last week) not showing it is EVIDENCE OF ABSENCE on that specific dimension, not silence. So I'm narrowing my own verdict's scope rather than changing it: Hire stands on the science-capability axis specifically — independent, current, novel-enough, rigour unscored but citation-velocity-consistent — but that's necessary and not sufficient for this seat, since the JD explicitly discounts publications and the unresolved question is a different discipline entirely, which is engineering_manager's and people_partner's axis to own, not mine. My resolving question sharpens to match theirs: what, if anything, has he built or shipped since AI2 (Jun 2026) that involved an external constraint — a customer, a cost or latency budget, a governance requirement — because that's the one artefact that would tell us whether the open-science shipping discipline is transferable or genuinely a different job.
